newsitem.title: CANADA: Avenor to issue 29 mln shares in Repap deal.
newsitem.headline: Avenor to issue 29 mln shares in Repap deal.

text.p: Avenor Inc said on Wednesday that it plans to issue 29 million new shares as part of its all-stock offer for all of Repap Enterprises Inc.

In a telephone conference call with reporters, Avenor President and Chief Executive Paul Gagne said the shares will be issued as part of Avenor's offer to exchange one newly issued Avenor common share for every 4.25 Repap shares.
Avenor officials said the value of the common share exchange is C$617 million, while the total value of the company's offer to buy Repap, including existing Repap debt, is about C$3.3 billion.
Gagne said that after the acquisition, which he expects to close by February 28, Avenor will have a debt-to-equity ratio of 59:41.
Gagne said Avenor would move "aggressively" to create synergies after the purchase, but he declined to indicate specifically which assets Avenor might divest.

In trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange mid-morning Wednesday, Avenor shares were down 2.50 to 18.70 on brisk volume of almost 900,000 shares. Also on the TSE, shares of Repap were down 1.05 to 4.45 on volume of more than 1.3 million shares.

Avenor Chief Financial Officer Denis Aubin said Avenor's offer translates into a value of about C$870 million to buy Repap's common shares and convertible debentures. Avenor will also assume about C$2.5 billion of Repap debt, bringing the value of the total transaction to about C$3.3 billion.
He said Avenor's common share exchange offer works out to a value of about C$5 for each Repap share.
Gagne said that he will remain as president and chief executive of Avenor and Michel Belanger will remain chairman. Repap Chairman and Chief Executive George Petty will become a director of Avenor.
Gagne declined to elaborate on the future role of Repap president Stephen Larsen.
Gagne said the combined Avenor and Repap will have sales of about C$5 billion annually, making it one of Canada's largest pulp and paper companies, second perhaps only to MacMillan Bloedel Ltd.
He said that one of the positive factors in the proposed acquisition is Repap's Canadian tax benefits, which include C$172 million of investment tax credits.
"By combining the two companies we will be able to make effective utilization of the tax attributes that Repap has," Gagne said.
